# Phase 15 gate report: the 3B stress model

**Status: complete. The gate deliverables are done (tests, experiment, this report, commit).**

Every result through Phase 14 is Llama-3.2-1B. The brief (§B8) named a 3B model as the stress case,
where KV is a larger share of VRAM: Llama-3.2-3B stores
114,688 bytes of KV per token against the 1B's
32,768. Its weights only fit as 4-bit nf4
(bitsandbytes); the KV stays bf16, so every rung sees the same cache format as on the 1B. The
reference is the 3B model's own full cache under the same 4-bit weights, so a retention measures a
policy's effect on this model, not quantization's.

## Gate checklist (CLAUDE.md rule 3)

- [x] **Tests run.** `pytest`, all passing, including `tests/test_phase15_analysis.py` (a prompt is
  paired across models only if both runs recorded the same needle values at the same position; the
  joint bootstrap sees a real model gap and does not invent one).
- [x] **Real experiment run.** `scripts/02_policy_quality.py --config configs/phase15.yaml
  --skip-block-full --skip-teacher-forced`, detached from a worktree pinned at the commit under
  test.
- [x] **Phase doc written.** This file.
- [x] **Committed and pushed.**

## Design, and what did not fit

16,384 tokens, NIAH (single, multi-key, multi-value needles
at five depths, samples 0-2): exactly the prompts Phase 8 ran on the 1B model at this context. The
analysis checks the pairing rather than assuming it, and all
45 of
45 prompts carry the same needles at the same
token positions in both runs. Rungs 2, 4, 5 and 6. The 1B run did not include rung 4, so H2O-style
eviction has 3B numbers only.

32K was ruled out before this phase by a feasibility check (the full reference spilled into shared
memory). The design then lost three more things to VRAM, each found by a smoke test or a failed run
before any 3B answer was read, and each recorded in `configs/phase15.yaml`:

- **Spare tier slots.** Rung 6 normally keeps VRAM slots for twice its selection. At the loose
  budgets that is every block, a second full-size cache beside the reference, and building it ran
  out of memory. The run uses no spare slots. Spare slots change how often blocks are fetched
  (Phase 4), not which blocks are attended, and the check below confirms rung 6 still answers as
  rung 5 does.
- **The 75% budget and the 100% block-pool control.** Every rung that copies KV adds that fraction
  of the cache again beside the reference, and at 75% decode ran out of memory on allocator
  fragmentation. The block-pool control is a whole second copy, dropped as at 64K on the 1B
  (Phase 8). 75% is where every rung sat nearest the full cache on the 1B, so it is the least
  informative budget to lose.
- **Teacher-forced divergence.** The first full run finished all of NIAH and then ran out of memory
  in the teacher-forced pass, whose longer sequence (context plus a scored continuation) no longer
  fit. The driver writes results only at the end, so that pass's NIAH answers were lost too, and
  NIAH was rerun on its own. No 3B perplexity or KL is reported.

The run itself stayed in dedicated VRAM. Its shared-memory growth matches the tier's pinned host
pools scaled by the model's KV size, as in Phase 8.

## 1. Query-aware selection keeps much more of the 3B model's accuracy at tight budgets

100.0% of these prompts and the 1B's
85.6%. The model difference gets a bootstrap CI that
resamples prompts jointly for both models. The last two columns repeat it on only the
32 prompts both full caches answer
completely. That check was added after the results were read (see below).

**Rungs 5 and 6 retain more on the 3B model at the two tightest budgets, and the gap widens as the
budget tightens.** At 12.5%, Quest-style selection keeps
92.8% of the 3B model's accuracy against
66.2% of the 1B's. At 6.25% it keeps
76.7% against
42.9%. Both differences are resolved on
all prompts and on the common set. At 25% the all-prompts interval straddles zero, but the
common-set interval
(+2.3 pp to
+21.9 pp) does not.

**No model difference is detected for the window.** On all prompts the 3B window looks slightly worse
at three budgets, but the common-set check removes that: every window interval there touches zero
(at 50%, -4.7 pp to
+0.0 pp). The all-prompts deficit
came from the denominators. On the multi-key and multi-value prompts outside the common set, the
1B's full cache earns only partial credit, so the 1B's retention there is a window score divided by
a small number, while the 3B's full cache earns full credit on the same prompts. In absolute terms
the 3B window scores slightly more than the 1B window on those prompts. This is why the common-set
check was added. It is post hoc, so it qualifies the all-prompts column
rather than replacing it.

**Why is not tested here.** The two models differ in more than size: the 3B has more layers, a
different query-to-KV head ratio and quantized weights. One reading consistent with the table: a
selector that ranks blocks by the current query does better when the model's own attention is more
concentrated on the evidence, while a window's loss is set by where the needle sits, not by the
model. Neither premise is measured here.

## 2. The ladder's order holds on the 3B model

The config fixed the expected order before the run: Quest-style selection ≥ H2O-style eviction ≥
window with sink, as on the 1B ladder. By point estimate it holds at every budget run:

| Budget | 3B, by point estimate | 1B, by point estimate |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 50% | rung 5 = rung 6 > rung 4 > rung 2 | rung 5 = rung 6 > rung 2 |
| 25% | rung 5 = rung 6 > rung 4 > rung 2 | rung 5 = rung 6 > rung 2 |
| 12.5% | rung 5 = rung 6 > rung 4 > rung 2 | rung 5 = rung 6 > rung 2 |
| 6.25% | rung 5 = rung 6 > rung 4 > rung 2 | rung 5 = rung 6 > rung 2 |

Rungs 5 and 6 tie because they answer identically (below). The rung-to-rung differences on the 3B
model were not tested.

## 3. The tier behaves the same under a quantized model

Rung 6 answered differently from rung 5 on
0 prompt-budget pairs,
matching the identity Phase 4 established on the 1B. Moving non-selected KV to pinned host memory
and fetching it on demand changes nothing the 3B model attends to. That holds here with no spare
slots, as it held on the 1B with them.

## What this changes

- **§B8's stress model is measured, at 16K and on NIAH only.** The headline's 32K and the
  teacher-forced measures did not fit on this card beside a full-size reference, a limit of the
  evaluation (it needs the reference resident), not of the tier.
- **Query-aware selection's tight-budget losses on the 1B are not a floor.** On the larger model,
  the same selection at the same fraction keeps much more. The 1B remains the harsher test, so the
  ladder's 1B numbers are conservative for this family, but one other model is not a trend.
- **The window's losses carry over.** No model difference is detected for position-based
  residency, so the case against it does not weaken on the larger model.
